The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

aThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

lThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

tThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

.The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

sThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

tThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

gThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

eThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

"The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

does not answer.

it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

iThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

tThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

lThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

does not answer.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

cThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

-The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

NThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

cThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

-The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

vThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

does not answer.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

eThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

JThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

fThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

EThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

nThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

oThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

aThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

iThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

iThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

eThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

tThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

tThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

yThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

cThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

eThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

nThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

sThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

PThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

oThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

nThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

rThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

nThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

dThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

does not answer.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

yThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

rThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

fThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

oThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

eThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

wThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

cThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

mThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

sThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

 The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

-The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

"The helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.

The helper reads the controllers from OpenVR on every 250 ms poll: each device of class
`Controller` with its `Prop_SerialNumber_String`, connected when its pose says so. The serial is the
one the disconnect request takes. A controller that turns off keeps its device index and serial, so
it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

it stays listed as not connected. A controller that has been off since SteamVR started is not
listed.

The helper sends every PC `{"type":"controllers","controllers":[{"serial":"96c863a69af3","connected":true}]}`
on connect and on every change. The list is sorted by serial, and empty while SteamVR on the headset
does not answer.

aThe helper opens that socket only for the request and closes it right after. While a socket that
sent `steam_connect` is open, the web server sends Steam UI's messages to it instead of to Steam UI,
such as `UpdateFrameUIs` for a new window. A window that opens meanwhile never shows in VR, and
the Frame's power button stops working. Steam UI gets its messages again as soon as the socket
closes.
